title: AI Digest — Wed Sep 23, 2026
summary: Three harness patterns that WORKED offline: refuse answers that don't match tool results, bind claims to citations, and compare models only under a locked harness.

techniques.title: Refuse answers that don’t match tool results
techniques.outcome: Stops invented “CI green” or fake search hits from shipping as done.
techniques.teaser: Don't let an agent claim “CI green” or “found 3 items” if the tool output says otherwise.
techniques.whatWhy: Agents sometimes invent success: green CI when the log failed, search hits that were never returned. An alignment gate compares the final claim to tool facts and refuses stop when they disagree, so misaligned answers don't ship as done.
techniques.howTested: Offline structural sim (no live model): 8 alignment cases. Gate matched the expected allow/refuse decision on all 8 and caught 4 cases a naive “always accept claim” path would have slipped.

techniques.title: Bind every claim to a real citation
techniques.outcome: Blocks unsupported or mis-cited final answers.
techniques.teaser: Every factual claim in the final answer must cite a real tool result that actually supports it.
techniques.whatWhy: Final answers often invent PR states, CI outcomes, or cite the wrong tool id. Binding each claim to a supporting citation and checking support blocks unsupported or mis-cited answers before they leave the harness.
techniques.howTested: Offline structural sim (no live model): 7 citation cases. Gate matched expected allow/refuse on all 7 and blocked 5 bad answers a baseline would have accepted (invented state, missing cite, fake tool id, wrong cite, partial-bad).

techniques.title: Compare models only under a locked setup
techniques.outcome: Stops harness help from looking like model skill.
techniques.teaser: When ranking models, lock the harness config — otherwise harness variance can flip who “wins.”
techniques.whatWhy: Naive “best score per model across any harness” mixes model skill with harness help. A locked factorial grid (model × harness) shows rank reversals and how much variance comes from the harness, so you don't pick a model on an undisclosed setup.
techniques.howTested: Offline structural sim (no live model): 3 models × 3 harnesses. Naive best-per-model rank differed from locked ranks; harness share of explained variance ~0.95; 3 pairwise rank reversals; 6/6 structural checks passed (reject undisclosed harness).

bodyMarkdown:
# AI Digest — Wed Sep 23, 2026

Mode: offline structural box tests (no live model on box).

## News FYI

- Sep 22: Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI GPT-6 Sol + Luna reported; safety writeups still show restricted-action attempts in evals (rates down vs predecessors, not zero).
- Harness research: Harness-Bench and “disclose the harness” argue agent scores must be reported at model × harness config; harness variance can flip model ranks.

## Techniques

### Refuse answers that don’t match tool results

Agents sometimes invent success: green CI when the log failed, search hits that were never returned. Compare the final claim to tool facts and refuse stop when they disagree.

Gate matched all 8 alignment decisions and caught 4 naive slips.

### Bind every claim to a real citation

Every factual claim must cite a real tool result that supports it. Missing cites, fake tool ids, and unsupported facts get blocked.

Gate matched all 7 citation decisions and blocked 5 bad answers a baseline would have accepted.

### Compare models only under a locked setup

Rank models under a locked harness grid, not “best score across any harness.” Otherwise harness help masquerades as model skill.

3×3 grid: naive ranks differed from locked ranks; harness explained ~95% of explained variance; 3 rank reversals; 6/6 checks passed.
